name: Glowing Ember
summary: At the Shrine of Eternal Flame, a Glowing Ember kindles the brazier for a shaman's trial. It comes from a Minor Manifestation of Fire on Durotar's crags.

sections.title: Core of the Flame
sections.body: A rising shaman drinks fire sapta to see the fiery spirits on the ridge near Telf Joolam. There, the initiate faces a Minor Manifestation of Fire. When the elemental falls, only a smoldering ember remains of its physical form. Raw elemental heat still pulses within it, carrying the living spark needed to awaken the sacred brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame.

sections.title: Igniting the Torch
sections.body: When the Glowing Ember enters the mountain brazier's cool basin, white-hot fire bursts to life. The brazier's flame lets the initiate light the Torch of the Dormant Flame. The torch binds fire's unruly essence in a vessel the initiate can carry down the mountain as proof of mastery over the elements.

faq.q: Where does the Glowing Ember come from?
faq.answer: You recover the ember from a defeated Minor Manifestation of Fire at the summit above the Shrine of Eternal Flame in Durotar.

faq.q: What is the ember used for?
faq.answer: You place the ember in the metal brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame. Its intense, rhythmic flame lights the ceremonial Torch of the Dormant Flame.

faq.q: Why do shamans need the fire sapta to acquire it?
faq.answer: The elemental spirits atop the mountain are beyond ordinary mortal sight. Drinking fire sapta attunes your senses to the elemental plane and reveals the Minor Manifestation of Fire, so you can challenge it.

faq.q: Who directs shamans to seek this ember?
faq.answer: Telf Joolam, a hermit in the crags of Durotar, brews the fire sapta and guides shaman initiates through the trial of defeating the flame spirit.

angles.text: As a shaman, you test your resolve against living fire in this rite of passage before commanding your totem.
